problem: Multi-hop KBQA needs a question-relevant subgraph as the reasoning scope, but a small subgraph may exclude the answer while a large one adds noise; existing retrieval is either heuristic or interwoven with reasoning, causing reasoning over partial subgraphs and bias when intermediate supervision is missing.
method: A trainable subgraph retriever (SR) decoupled from the reasoner: a question-path encoder scores candidate paths, top paths are expanded and induced into a question-relevant subgraph, and the retriever is pre-trained (weakly supervised and unsupervised) then fine-tuned end-to-end with feedback from the downstream reasoner (NSM). Plug-and-play with any subgraph-oriented KBQA model.
key_assumptions: Reasoning should be performed on a retrieved subgraph rather than the full KB.
Retriever quality can be improved by end-to-end feedback from the reasoner.
WebQSP and CWQ topic-centric subgraphs (2-hop / 4-hop) are representative reasoning scopes.
main_contribution: A decoupled, trainable subgraph retriever that improves both retrieval and QA performance and reaches state of the art when combined with NSM for embedding-based KBQA, with analyses of how subgraph size trades answer coverage against noise.
datasets: Freebase (whole KB; 2-hop/4-hop topic-centric subgraphs per question)
baselines: NSM (He et al., 2021) with existing retrieval methods
Prior heuristic / interwoven subgraph retrieval methods
Embedding-based KBQA methods (e.g., embeddings over the whole KB, per related-work comparison)
metrics: Hits@1 for QA (also answer coverage rate of retrieved subgraphs, retriever Hits@1)
results: SR achieves significantly better retrieval and QA performance than existing retrieval methods, and new state-of-the-art when combined with NSM for embedding-based KBQA; Figure 1 shows subgraph size strongly affects answer coverage and QA Hits@1 on WebQSP and CWQ. Exact numbers not extracted here.
limitations: No dedicated limitations or error-analysis section was found in the retrieved full text (searches for 'limitation', 'future work', 'error analysis' returned no passages).
Reasoning remains over an induced subgraph rather than an LLM trained with textual context; retrieval is question-centric, not passage-local to each training triple.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: SR selects a question-relevant subgraph at inference to reduce the reasoning space for an embedding-based reasoner; the idea instead attaches passage-local supporting triples to each target triple as an LLM supervised-fine-tuning signal. Both use a 'context subgraph', but SR's subgraph is question-centric and retrieved, whereas the idea's context graph is passage-local to the supervised triple and used as training supervision, with no repair or RL stage in SR.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.7 because both address limited/noisy context for multi-hop KGQA and explicitly discuss the trade-off between too-small and too-large subgraphs; method overlap 0.55 because subgraph construction is central to both but SR trains a retriever+embedding reasoner rather than an LLM, and does not attach context to a target triple's supervision; evaluation overlap 0.35 because it uses standard WebQSP/CWQ with Hits@1 while the idea's closest comparable setting is generated per-hop MCQ accuracy (and the idea leaves the benchmark open).
